1.title: Observing the Situation

story.title: Watching Before Joining
story.content: A child was observing a playground before joining. It's always smart to see who is playing and what the rules are before jumping into the game.
story.moral: Look carefully before acting to make smart choices.

1.activity: Before starting your next game, take 10 seconds to observe everything around you.

1.title: Planning & Strategy

story.title: The Strategic Plan
story.content: A child was planning team strategy. Instead of just running wildly, they thought of a plan to help their team win.
story.moral: Thinking and planning before action gives you a big advantage.

1.activity: What is one 'strategy' you use when playing your favorite game?

1.title: Knowing Your Team

story.title: Identifying Team Players
story.content: A child was identifying team players. They knew one friend was fast, another was strong, and another was smart. Together, they were an unbeatable team.
story.moral: Knowing what you and your friends are good at makes teamwork much easier.

1.activity: Name one thing you are really good at, and one thing your best friend is really good at.

1.title: Leadership & Guidance

story.title: Motivating the Team
story.content: The team captain was motivating players. Even when they felt tired, the leader's words made them feel proud and strong again.
story.moral: A good leader doesn't just give orders; they motivate and inspire others.

1.activity: What is one nice thing you can say to encourage a friend today?

1.title: Confidence in Strength

story.title: Feeling Ready
story.content: Instead of worrying, a child was feeling ready before the match. They knew they had practiced hard and prepared well.
story.moral: Trusting your preparation pushes away your fears.

1.activity: Count on your fingers 3 things that make you a strong person.

1.title: Preparing for Action

story.title: Final Preparation Moment
story.content: A child was in the final preparation moment before starting. They tied their shoes tight, drank water, and took deep breaths.
story.moral: Taking time to prepare makes the actual task much easier.

1.activity: What is your routine to 'get ready' before you go to school or sleep?

1.title: Energy & Excitement

story.title: The Team Cheer
story.content: There was huge excitement in the team cheer moment. High energy helps wake up your body and mind for action.
story.moral: Excitement and high energy can give you the push you need to start.

1.activity: Do 5 jumping jacks right now to build some high energy!

1.title: Showing Presence

story.title: Entering the Stage Boldly
story.content: A child was entering the stage boldly. They stood tall and smiled. Even before they spoke a word, everyone believed in them.
story.moral: Standing tall and confident helps you believe in yourself, and helps others believe in you too.

1.activity: Stand up straight, push your chest out slightly, and hold your head high!

1.title: Readiness & Focus

story.title: Waiting for Your Turn
story.content: A child was waiting for their turn in a game. They held their bat ready, eyes on the ball, completely focused.
story.moral: Stay alert and focused so you are ready when it's your time to act.

1.activity: What do you do to stay patient and ready when you have to wait for your turn?

1.title: Final Observation

story.title: Looking Before Making a Move
story.content: The child was looking before making a move. Instead of just running blindly, they checked the whole field one last time.
story.moral: Final observation ensures you have the full picture before you act.

1.activity: Before starting your next task, take one last look to make sure you have everything you need.

1.title: Overwhelmed by Emotions
1.micro_theme: Fear and confusion can take over

story.title: The Big Stage Fright
story.content: A child named Rohan was so excited for the school talent show. But right before stepping on stage, he looked at the huge crowd and completely froze! Fear and confusion took over, just like how Arjuna felt when he saw everyone lined up to fight.
story.moral: It is completely normal to feel overwhelmed by big emotions when facing something scary.

1.activity: Draw a face showing what 'overwhelmed' looks like, and another showing 'calm'.

1.title: Physical Signs of Fear

story.title: The Shaking Knees
story.content: Before his big math exam, Sam's hands got sweaty and his knees literally started shaking. He felt so weak he sat down. When we are extremely nervous, our body reacts! Arjuna's bow even slipped from his hands because he was so nervous.
story.moral: Your body reacts to your thoughts. Calming your mind will calm your body.

1.activity: When you feel nervous, where do you feel it in your body? (Tummy? Hands?)

1.title: Losing Clarity

story.title: The Ice Cream Dilemma
story.content: Mia was at the ice cream shop. There were 50 flavors! Her mind got so confused she just couldn't pick. The longer she looked, the harder it got. When our mind is confused, even simple decisions seem impossible.
story.moral: When you are confused, take a deep breath and keep things simple.

1.activity: What do you do when you can't decide between two fun things?

1.title: Avoiding Responsibility

story.title: The Messy Room
story.content: Leo's mom told him to clean his very messy room. Instead, Leo said, 'I don't even care about having a clean room anymore!' and tried to avoid doing it. Running away from duty doesn't fix the problem; it just leaves the room messy.
story.moral: We must face our responsibilities, even when they seem hard or unpleasant.

1.activity: Name one chore you don't like doing, but you know you have to.

1.title: Emotional Attachment

story.title: The Spelling Bee
story.content: Tina had to compete against her best friend in the final round of the spelling bee. She didn't want to spell the word right because she didn't want her friend to lose. Her attachment to her friend clouded her judgment of simply doing her best.
story.moral: Sometimes our love for others makes it hard to do what we are supposed to do.

1.activity: Is it better to let your friend win, or for both of you to do your absolute best?

1.title: Conflict of Relationships

story.title: The Broken Vase
story.content: Jay saw his older brother accidentally break a vase. His mother asked who did it. Jay loved his brother, but he knew lying was wrong. Choosing between doing what is right and protecting someone you love is a very hard choice.
story.moral: Always choose truth and duty, even when it involves people you care about.

1.activity: What would you do if your friend asked you to keep a secret that wasn't safe?

1.title: Refusing to Act

story.title: Giving Up Early
story.content: When Neha saw the huge puzzle with 1000 pieces, she just sat on the floor and said, 'I am not doing this!' She gave up before she even tried placing one piece. Refusing to act guarantees you will never finish.
story.moral: You can't succeed if you refuse to even start.

1.activity: Think of a time you wanted to give up before trying. How did you push through?

1.title: Fear of Consequences

story.title: The Nervous Goalie
story.content: Max was the goalie for his soccer team. He was terrified of missing the ball and making his team lose. Because he was so focused on the fear of making a mistake, he wasn't paying attention to the game!
story.moral: Focusing too much on 'what if things go wrong' stops you from doing things right.

1.activity: Say out loud: 'I am not afraid of making mistakes, I learn from them!'

1.title: Thinking Too Much

story.title: The Scary Shadows
story.content: At night, Lily saw a weird shadow on her wall. She started imagining it was a monster, then a dragon, then aliens! She overthought it so much she couldn't sleep. Her dad turned on the light—it was just a jacket. Overthinking creates stress that isn't real.
story.moral: Don't let your imagination create problems that aren't there.

1.activity: When you start overthinking, name 3 things you can see in the room to ground yourself.

1.title: Confused Judgment

story.title: The Mixed-Up Map
story.content: Aya tried to read a map while riding a bumpy, fast train. Everything looked blurry and she got totally confused about where to go. When our mind is bumpy with emotions, our judgment gets blurry and we can't tell right from wrong.
story.moral: Calm your mind first, then decide what is right.

1.activity: Take a deep breath and count to 5. Notice how your mind slows down.

1.title: Negative Thinking Spiral
1.micro_theme: One negative thought leads to another

story.title: The Bad Day Trap
story.content: Sam spilled his juice. Then he thought, 'Today is terrible.' Because he was grumpy, he forgot his homework. Then he thought, 'I am the worst!' One bad thought led to another until he was stuck in a spiral of worry.
story.moral: Stop the spiral! One bad thing doesn't mean everything is bad.

1.activity: If you have a bad thought, how can you change it into a good thought immediately?

1.title: Fear of Loss

story.title: The Block Tower
story.content: Zara built a tall block tower. She was so afraid of it falling over that she wouldn't let anyone come near her, and she stopped having fun building it. Fear of losing something ruins the joy of having it.
story.moral: Don't let the fear of losing stop you from enjoying what you have.

1.activity: Think of a time you lost a game but still had fun playing.

1.title: Losing Confidence

story.title: The Steep Hill
story.content: Ravi was riding his bike up a hill. It looked so steep! Before he even tried pedaling hard, his mind said 'I can't do this,' and he put his feet down. He gave up in his mind before his legs even got tired.
story.moral: Your mind gives up way before your body does. Stay confident!

1.activity: Stand up tall like a superhero and say, 'I can do hard things!'

1.title: Complete Withdrawal

story.title: Sitting Out
story.content: In gym class, the teacher announced a complicated new game. Instead of trying to learn it, Maya just went and sat on the bench. She completely shut down. Arjuna did the same thing when he sat down in his chariot and dropped his bow.
story.moral: It is okay to ask for help when things are hard, but completely quitting helps no one.

1.activity: When you want to quit, who can you ask for help instead?

2.title: Don't Be Weak

story.title: The Big Stage Fright
story.content: Arjun was feeling very scared. He had to go on stage for the school play, but his legs were shaking. He felt like he couldn't do it. But then, his teacher reminded him: 'You practiced hard. Don't let fear make you weak. Think clearly about how well you know your lines!' By understanding the situation clearly instead of panicking, Arjun found his courage.
story.moral: When we feel helpless, stepping back to think clearly gives us strength.

2.activity: Think of a time you were scared to try something new. What did you do to overcome the fear?

2.title: Life Changes Naturally

story.title: The Changing Seasons
story.content: Riya loved summer. She loved the warm sun and playing outside late. When autumn came and the leaves fell, she felt sad. But her grandmother told her, 'Look at the trees. They are resting. Soon, winter will come, and then spring with new flowers.' Riya realized that just like we grow from a baby to a big kid, everything in life changes, and that is perfectly normal.
story.moral: Change is natural. We grow, seasons change, and life moves forward beautifully.

2.activity: Draw a picture of a tree in summer and a tree in winter. How are they different?

2.title: Stay Strong in Difficulty
2.micro_theme: Stay steady in happiness and sadness

story.title: The Soccer Game
story.content: Sam loved playing soccer. Last week his team won, and he cheered loudly! But this week, his team lost the finals. Sam was very upset and wanted to quit. His coach said, 'A true champion stays strong whether they win or lose. You learn from both!' Sam took a deep breath, shook hands with the other team, and decided to practice harder for next time.
story.moral: Be like a strong mountain. Don't let winning make you too proud, or losing make you too sad.

2.activity: What is one thing you can tell yourself next time you lose a game so you don't feel too sad?

2.title: What is Real

story.title: The Shiny Toy
story.content: Maya wanted the big, shiny plastic toy at the store, even though her mom said it would break easily. Maya insisted and got it. Two days later, it broke! Meanwhile, her old wooden blocks were still there, ready to build a big castle. Maya learned that flashy things don't last long, but real, strong things (like good toys and good friends) last forever.
story.moral: Focus on things that are real and lasting, not just things that look shiny for a moment.

2.activity: Name one thing you have that is 'real' and lasts a long time (like family, love, or knowledge).

2.title: Soul Never Dies
2.micro_theme: You are more than your body

story.title: The Unbreakable Light
story.content: Imagine you have a flashlight. If you change the batteries or change the plastic case, the light inside is still the same light. In the same way, we have a body that changes as we grow, but the real 'us' inside—our soul—is like that light. It never breaks, it never dies, it is always shining bright!
story.moral: Your body changes, but the real you inside is forever.

2.activity: Close your eyes and imagine a bright, warm light inside your heart. That is your soul!

2.title: Change is Natural
2.micro_theme: Old things go, new things come

story.title: The Old Favorite Shirt
story.content: Leo had a favorite superhero shirt. He wore it everywhere! But one day, it got too small and ripped. Leo was crying. His dad bought him a brand new, bigger superhero shirt. His dad said, 'When old clothes tear, we just get new ones.' The soul does exactly the same thing. When a body gets old, the soul gets a brand new body to continue its journey.
story.moral: Don't be afraid when things get old and go away; it just means something new is coming.

2.activity: Think of a toy or piece of clothing you outgrew. Who did you give it to?

2.title: Do Your Duty
2.micro_theme: Do what is right, even if hard

story.title: Homework Before Play
story.content: Aarav heard his friends playing outside. He wanted to run out so badly! But he had a math assignment due tomorrow. He knew his 'duty' as a student was to finish his homework first. It was hard to stay inside, but he focused, finished his math quickly, and then went out to play with a clear, happy mind. He did his duty!
story.moral: Doing your duty (what you are supposed to do) is always the right choice, even when it's tough.

2.activity: What is one 'duty' you have at home? (Like cleaning your room or doing homework).

2.title: Focus on Effort
2.micro_theme: Do your best, don't worry about result

story.title: The Art Contest
story.content: Sia was painting a picture for an art contest. She kept thinking, 'What if I don't win first prize?' This made her nervous, and her hands shook, ruining her painting. Her teacher said, 'Just focus on enjoying the painting. Don't worry about the prize.' Sia started over, painting just for fun. It turned out beautiful!
story.moral: You only have control over your effort, not the result. Do your best and forget the rest!

2.activity: Next time you do a test, tell yourself: 'I will just do my best, I won't worry about the marks!'

2.title: Stay Balanced

story.title: The Tower of Blocks
story.content: Kabir was building a huge tower of blocks. He got it really high and felt very proud. But then, his little sister accidentally knocked it over! Instead of yelling or crying, Kabir took a deep breath. 'That's okay,' he said. 'Now I get to build it again, even better.' He stayed balanced in his mind.
story.moral: A wise person stays calm when things go perfectly, and stays calm when things fall apart.

2.activity: Practice taking three slow, deep breaths to find your balance right now.

2.title: Smart Work Matters

story.title: The Rushed Project
story.content: Jay had to build a birdhouse. He wanted to finish fast so he could play video games. He glued the wood quickly and it looked crooked. His friend Tara took her time, used the right tools, and built it carefully with a calm mind. Tara's birdhouse looked amazing and lasted a long time. Jay realized that doing things with a calm, focused attitude is the true smart work.
story.moral: Yoga is excellence in action. When you work with a calm, peaceful mind, your work becomes excellent.

2.activity: Think of a chore you usually rush. How can you do it with more focus next time?

2.title: Clear Thinking

story.title: The Lost Map
story.content: Emma and her family were lost in the forest. Her brother was running around confused, saying 'Go left! No, go right!' Emma stopped, sat down, and looked at the map quietly. By clearing her mind of panic and confusion, she found the right path back home.
story.moral: When your mind is clear and not confused by too many loud thoughts, you make the right choices.

2.activity: When you feel confused, sit quietly for 1 minute before making a decision.

2.title: Who is a Calm Person?

story.title: The Unbothered Frog
story.content: In a pond, all the little fishes were panicking because a loud boat went by. The water was splashing everywhere! But a wise old frog just sat on his lily pad, completely still and peaceful. He didn't let the splashing bother him. A calm person is just like that frog—peaceful inside, even when things are crazy outside.
story.moral: A person with steady wisdom doesn't let big desires or outside noise disturb their peace.

2.activity: Can you sit as still and quiet as a wise frog for 30 seconds?

2.title: Control Senses

story.title: The Tortoise and the Noise
story.content: When a tortoise sees danger or too much noise, what does it do? It pulls its legs and head inside its shell! When Neil was trying to read a book, the TV was loud and toys were everywhere. Like a tortoise, Neil 'pulled in' his attention. He looked only at his book and ignored the distractions.
story.moral: We must learn to pull our senses away from distractions, just like a tortoise pulls its limbs into its shell.

2.activity: Next time you study, pretend to be a tortoise pulling your focus away from everything else.

2.title: Danger of Distraction
2.micro_theme: Mind can slip if not careful

story.title: The Slippery Path
story.content: Rohan was walking on a narrow, slippery path holding a cup of water. He was doing great until he looked away to watch a butterfly. Woops! He slipped and spilled the water. The mind is like that. Even if you are trying to be good and focused, if you let your senses get distracted by every shiny thing, you will lose your balance.
story.moral: Keep your focus steady, or your senses will pull you away like wild horses.

2.activity: Try balancing on one foot. See how you fall if you look around too much?

2.title: From Desire to Trouble
2.micro_theme: Too much desire leads to anger

story.title: The Cookie Monster
story.content: Dev kept thinking about the chocolate cookies in the jar. He thought about them so much that he really, really desired them. When his mom said 'No cookies before dinner,' his desire turned into anger! He threw a tantrum and completely forgot how to be a good boy. Thinking too much about things we want leads to anger and losing our wisdom.
story.moral: Desire leads to anger, anger leads to confusion, and confusion ruins our good sense.

2.activity: When you want something really badly and can't have it, try thinking about something completely different!

2.title: Peaceful Living

story.title: The Gentle Stream
story.content: A wild, rushing river crashes into rocks and makes a huge mess. But a gentle stream flows peacefully through the forest. When we control our likes and dislikes (like not crying for a toy, or not screaming when we eat vegetables), our mind becomes like the gentle stream. We feel so peaceful and happy inside.
story.moral: By controlling our mind and senses, we find true peace.

2.activity: Describe what a 'peaceful mind' feels like to you. Is it like a quiet room? Or a soft cloud?

2.title: No Peace Without Control

story.title: The Boat in the Wind
story.content: A small boat was on the ocean. The sailor didn't steer the boat, so the wind blew it left, right, and in circles! The sailor felt dizzy and unhappy. Our mind is the boat, and our senses are the wind. If we don't steer our mind with focus, our senses will blow us all over the place, and we will never find happiness.
story.moral: An unfocused mind is carried away by the senses, just like a boat is carried away by the wind.

2.activity: Be the captain of your mind! Say 'I am in control of my focus!'

2.title: Different Thinking

story.title: The Night Owl and the Crow
story.content: While all the other birds sleep at night, the wise owl is awake and sees things clearly in the dark. While all the other kids were fighting over a silly toy, Ananya stepped back and decided to read a book instead. What everyone else thought was 'important' (the toy), Ananya realized was silly. She thought differently, like the wise owl.
story.moral: A wise person finds peace in things that regular people ignore, and ignores the silly things people fight over.

2.activity: Think of a time you walked away from an argument because you knew it was silly.

2.title: Desireless Mind

story.title: The Ocean and the Rivers
story.content: Thousands of rivers flow into the ocean every day, but the ocean never overflows. It stays calm and majestic. People will always offer us things, and we will always see new toys or games. If we act like the ocean, taking them in but never feeling greedy or disturbed, we will always be at peace.
story.moral: True peace comes when you are completely satisfied inside, without constantly craving more things.

2.activity: Imagine you are the deep, calm ocean. Nothing can disturb your peace.

2.title: Ultimate Peace

story.title: The Joy of Being Free
story.content: Once a bird realized it was no longer in a cage, it flew high into the sky, feeling absolute joy and peace. When we stop being trapped by 'I want this' and 'This is mine', our mind becomes completely free like that bird. We reach a state of divine peace that lasts forever.
story.moral: Dropping the 'I' and 'Mine' feeling brings the ultimate spiritual peace.

2.activity: Share one thing you are grateful for today.

15.title: The Tree of Life
15.micro_theme: Life is like a growing tree

story.title: The Upside-Down Tree
story.content: Imagine a magical tree where the roots are in the sky and the branches grow downwards! The roots in the sky represent our connection to the divine, and the branches spreading out are the world we live in. We are all leaves on this giant, magical tree of life.
story.moral: We are connected to something much higher, even if we are busy playing in the branches.

15.activity: Draw an upside-down tree! Put the roots at the top of your paper.

15.title: Detach from Illusion

story.title: The Heavy Backpack
story.content: Rahul went hiking but filled his backpack with rocks just because they looked shiny. Soon, he was too tired to climb. His guide told him to empty the rocks so he could reach the top. To grow, we have to cut our attachment to heavy, unnecessary things.
story.moral: Letting go of distractions and silly attachments makes your journey much lighter.

15.activity: What is one 'heavy rock' (like playing too many video games) you can put down?

15.title: Search for Truth

story.title: The Treasure Hunt
story.content: Ahaana had a map to a hidden treasure. Many people told her to stop and just play in the mud, but she kept searching for the real treasure. Seeking the ultimate truth is like a great treasure hunt for your soul.
story.moral: Never stop searching for what is truly real and important in life.

15.activity: If you could ask the smartest person in the universe one question, what would it be?

15.title: Reaching the Highest Goal

story.title: The Clean Mirror
story.content: Aria wanted to see the stars in her mirror, but it was covered in dust. She cleaned it wiping away the dirt, and finally saw a perfect reflection of the night sky! When we clean our minds from pride and anger, we reflect the highest truth.
story.moral: A pure, clean mind can understand the highest goals in the universe.

15.activity: Name one good habit that helps keep your mind 'clean' and happy.

15.title: Inner Light

story.title: The Glowing Heart
story.content: The sun lights up the day, and the moon lights up the night. But there is a place that doesn't need the sun or moon to be bright—the spiritual world! That same pure, glowing light is deep inside your heart right now.
story.moral: You don't need outside things to shine; your soul is naturally bright.

15.activity: Close your eyes and picture a warm, glowing sun right in the center of your chest.

15.title: Soul's Journey

story.title: The Traveler
story.content: Imagine a traveler moving from one city to another, taking a little suitcase with them. The soul is just like that traveler! When one adventure (life) ends, the soul travels to a new body to start a brand new adventure.
story.moral: Life is an ongoing journey of learning for your soul.

15.activity: If your soul is a traveler, what is one good thing you want to pack in your suitcase?

15.title: Carrying Impressions

story.title: The Wind and the Flowers
story.content: When the wind blows over a rose garden, it carries the sweet smell of roses everywhere it goes. Our soul is like the wind. It carries the 'smell' of our good habits and bad habits from one life to the next.
story.moral: Make sure you surround yourself with good habits, so your soul carries a sweet fragrance!

15.activity: What 'sweet fragrance' (good habit) are you known for? (Being kind, helpful?)

15.title: Seeing with Awareness

story.title: The Magic Painting
story.content: Two kids looked at a painting. One just saw splashes of paint. The other kid looked closer and realized it was a beautiful picture of a galaxy! People who don't pay attention miss the magic of the soul, but those with awareness see it clearly.
story.moral: Look at the world with deep awareness, not just with your eyes.

15.activity: Look at something in your room very closely. What is a detail you never noticed before?

15.title: Energy in Everything

story.title: The Power of the Sun
story.content: Where does the energy in your food come from? The sun! The Divine energy is in the sun making plants grow, and it is in the earth holding everything together. That same amazing energy is keeping you alive right now.
story.moral: Everything in nature is powered by the same incredible, divine energy.

15.activity: Next time you eat a vegetable, thank the sun and the earth for giving it energy!

15.title: Nourishment & Growth

story.title: The Engine's Fuel
story.content: A car needs good fuel to run properly. In our bodies, a special divine fire (digestion) helps process the food we eat to give us strength! What we put into our bodies—good food, and good thoughts—shapes who we become.
story.moral: Nourish your body with healthy food, and your mind with positive thoughts.

15.activity: What is your favorite healthy food that gives you energy?

15.title: Source of Memory & Knowledge

story.title: The Quiet Whisper
story.content: When Leo couldn't remember the answer to a test, he closed his eyes and got very quiet. Suddenly, the answer popped into his head! The divine is seated in all our hearts, helping us remember, learn, and understand.
story.moral: True knowledge and memory come from the spark of the divine inside you.

15.activity: Close your eyes and listen carefully. What is the quietest sound you can hear right now?

15.title: Temporary vs Permanent

story.title: The Sandcastle and the Ocean
story.content: A sandcastle looks great, but it washes away with the tide—it is temporary. But the ocean itself is always there—it is permanent. In our world, bodies and toys change, but the highest truth and the soul are permanent, like the ocean.
story.moral: Learn to tell the difference between things that change and things that last forever.

15.activity: Name one thing that changes (like the weather) and one thing that doesn't (like your family's love).

15.title: The Supreme Reality
15.micro_theme: There is something higher than all

story.title: The King of the Castle
story.content: In a great kingdom, there are many workers, knights, and builders, but above all of them is the wise, caring King who watches over everything. In the universe, beyond all changing things and unchanging souls, is the Supreme Reality holding everything in love.
story.moral: There is a supreme, loving force that connects and supports the entire universe.

15.activity: Look up at the sky and imagine how huge the universe is!

15.title: True Understanding

story.title: The Puzzle Complete
story.content: For a long time, Maya had pieces of a puzzle. It was confusing! But when she finally put the last piece in, she saw the whole beautiful picture. Knowing the Supreme Reality is like finishing the puzzle of life—suddenly, everything makes sense.
story.moral: When you truly understand life's biggest truths, you act with pure wisdom.

15.activity: What is one 'big truth' you have learned from the Bhagavad Gita so far?

15.title: Final Wisdom

story.title: The Happy Heart
story.content: After learning all about the tree of life, the soul's journey, and the energy in everything, a young boy felt completely at peace. He wasn't worried about small things anymore. He had found the secret knowledge that makes a heart truly full and content.
story.moral: Understanding these spiritual truths brings perfect peace and joy to your life.

15.activity: Smile the biggest smile you can, knowing that the universe is a beautiful, magical place!
